sentences.en: Hello, hello, hello, and welcome to English Learning for Curious Minds, by Leonardo English, the show where you can listen to fascinating stories and learn weird and wonderful things about the world at the same time as improving your English.
sentences.zh: 哈喽，哈喽，哈喽，欢迎收听由 Leonardo English 制作的 English Learning for Curious Minds。在这个节目中，你可以一边听引人入胜的故事，了解世界上各种奇妙有趣的事物，一边提高你的英语水平。

sentences.en: I'm Alastair Budge, and today we have an unusual type of episode.
sentences.zh: 我是 Alastair Budge，今天我们要播出一期不同寻常的节目。

sentences.en: I’m not going to talk about a person’s life, a historical event, or some other weird and wonderful thing going on in the world.
sentences.zh: 我不打算讲某个人的生平、历史事件，或者世界上正在发生的其他奇妙有趣的事情。

sentences.en: Today, I’m going to talk to you about how I choose, research, write and produce podcast episodes, and how this process has changed over the past almost six years of doing so.
sentences.zh: 今天，我要和大家聊聊我是如何选题、研究、撰写和制作播客节目的，以及在过去近六年的时间里，这个过程发生了怎样的变化。

sentences.en: I’ve had quite a few requests for this type of episode, and a few weeks ago, I got it again from an interesting Brazilian member called Itamar.
sentences.zh: 我收到过不少关于这类节目的请求，几周前，一位名叫 Itamar 的有趣的巴西会员再次提出了这个建议。

sentences.en: So, Itamar, and to everyone else listening to this, I hope you’ll enjoy this slightly meta type of episode.
sentences.zh: 所以，Itamar，还有每一位正在收听节目的听众，希望你们会喜欢这期有点“元”风格的节目。

sentences.en: I’m also going to share a bunch of things I found out about the kind of people who listen to this podcast from a recent survey, so I think you might find that interesting, too.
sentences.zh: 我还将分享一些从最近的调查中发现的关于本节目听众群体的信息，我想你们也会对此感兴趣的。

sentences.en: OK then, let’s get right into it. Depending on the way you calculate it, there are almost 5 million different podcasts.
sentences.zh: 好了，让我们直接进入正题。根据计算方式的不同，目前大约有 500 万个不同的播客。

sentences.en: Not individual podcast episodes; 5 million podcasts, 5 million different shows.
sentences.zh: 不是指单集节目，而是 500 万个播客频道，500 万个不同的节目。

sentences.en: As I’m sure you know, there are podcasts about everything: comedy, TV shows, business, football, knitting, fishing, obscure historical periods, and, lest I forget, podcasts that help you learn a language.
sentences.zh: 相信大家都知道，播客的主题无所不包：喜剧、电视节目、商业、足球、编织、钓鱼、冷门的历史时期，当然，还有帮助你学习语言的播客。

sentences.en: English Learning for Curious Minds–this podcast–is one of those.
sentences.zh: English Learning for Curious Minds——也就是本节目——就是其中之一。

sentences.en: Of course, it isn’t the only one. There are tonnes of different podcasts that help you learn English, and they tend to follow similar formats.
sentences.zh: 当然，它不是唯一的一个。有很多不同的英语学习播客，它们往往遵循类似的模式。

sentences.en: Some are conversation-based, with two teachers having a conversation about anything from their personal lives to a particular element of English grammar or language.
sentences.zh: 有些是以对话为基础的，两位老师会聊各种话题，从个人生活到特定的英语语法或语言要素。

sentences.en: Others might be one person giving motivational advice, or giving what’s essentially an English lesson in an audio format.
sentences.zh: 还有一些可能是一个人提供励志建议，或者以音频形式讲授英语课。

sentences.en: This one is a little different. My approach right from the start has always been to present an interesting and thought-provoking subject in a way that allows you to learn English through listening to the episode, and allows you to learn weird and wonderful things about the world at the same time as you improve your English.
sentences.zh: 这个节目有点不同。从一开始，我的方法就是呈现一个有趣且发人深省的主题，让你在听节目的过程中学习英语，在提高英语水平的同时，了解世界上奇妙有趣的事情。

sentences.en: This is now episode 565, so I have had quite a bit of practice making them.
sentences.zh: 现在已经是第 565 期了，所以我已经积累了相当丰富的制作经验。

sentences.en: And in this meta episode, I’ll tell you what I’ve learned and what the process of making an episode looks like now.
sentences.zh: 在这期“元”节目中，我将告诉大家我学到了什么，以及现在的节目制作流程是怎样的。

sentences.en: So, let’s go back to the start. When I first started, almost six years ago now, I had absolutely no idea what I was doing.
sentences.zh: 那么，让我们回到起点。大约六年前我刚开始做的时候，我完全不知道自己在做什么。

sentences.en: I had quite a good idea of what I wanted the finished product to look like–a 15- to 20-minute episode that was both interesting and helped people improve their English–but I didn’t have much of an idea about how to actually make one.
sentences.zh: 我对成品的构思很清晰——一期 15 到 20 分钟的节目，既有趣又能帮助人们提高英语——但我对具体怎么做却没什么头绪。

sentences.en: So…I just started, and figured I’d make it up as I went along.
sentences.zh: 所以……我就直接开始了，想着边做边摸索。

sentences.en: I chose some topics that I thought might be interesting, I did a bunch of research into them, and I pulled up Google Docs and just started typing.
sentences.zh: 我选了一些我觉得可能有趣的话题，做了一堆研究，然后打开 Google Docs 就开始写。

sentences.en: When I thought they were good enough, I recorded them using a microphone I borrowed from a friend.
sentences.zh: 当我觉得写得差不多了，我就用从朋友那里借来的麦克风录音。

sentences.en: Then I listened to them again and…I thought they sounded awful.
sentences.zh: 然后我回听了一下……我觉得听起来糟透了。

sentences.en: Firstly, like most people, I really didn’t like the sound of my own voice.
sentences.zh: 首先，和大多数人一样，我真的很不喜欢自己声音听起来的样子。

sentences.en: And secondly, I thought the content of the episodes themselves sounded dull.
sentences.zh: 其次，我觉得节目内容本身听起来很枯燥。

sentences.en: I wouldn’t want to listen to them, so why should anyone else?
sentences.zh: 连我自己都不想听，别人为什么要听呢？

sentences.en: In fact, I never released these early episodes.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我从未发布过这些早期的节目。

sentences.en: They were on topics I now realise were pretty difficult to make interesting in an audio-only format: there was one on how black holes work, and another one on how the international bond market works.
sentences.zh: 它们的主题我现在意识到很难仅通过音频形式讲得有趣：有一期是关于黑洞如何运作的，另一期是关于国际债券市场如何运作的。

sentences.en: Interesting and important subjects, sure, but quite hard to turn into an interesting topic for someone at B1 or B2 level.
sentences.zh: 这些主题当然很有趣也很重要，但很难转化成适合 B1 或 B2 水平学习者的有趣话题。

sentences.en: So, I scrapped them - they simply never saw the light of day.
sentences.zh: 所以，我把它们废弃了——它们从未面世。

sentences.en: I decided to choose some slightly easier subjects to tackle, and things that I was more familiar with, and got cracking.
sentences.zh: 我决定选一些稍微容易处理、我也更熟悉的主题，然后就开始干了。

sentences.en: That was in December 2019, coming on 6 years ago now, and I have just kept going, with a few changes and improvements along the way.
sentences.zh: 那是在 2019 年 12 月，快 6 年前了，我一直坚持到现在，期间也做了一些改变和改进。

sentences.en: So, how does it work now? Well, first comes the idea for the topic.
sentences.zh: 那么，现在的流程是怎样的呢？首先是选题构思。

sentences.en: If you are a seasoned listener to this show, you’ll know that we’ve covered a lot of different subjects.
sentences.zh: 如果你是本节目的老听众，你会知道我们涵盖了许多不同的主题。

sentences.en: There’s been everything from episodes about the life of disappeared English aristocrats through to stories about the Vikings, how recycling works, conspiracies from ancient times, the list goes on.
sentences.zh: 从失踪的英国贵族生平，到维京人的故事、回收如何运作、古代阴谋论，不胜枚举。

sentences.en: There are only really three things that need to be true for me to decide that they are worthy of an episode.
sentences.zh: 只有满足三个条件，我才会决定某个主题值得做成一期节目。

sentences.en: Firstly, I need to find the subject interesting.
sentences.zh: 第一，我必须觉得这个主题有趣。

sentences.en: Whether that means it’s an interesting story about a period of history, about someone who lived a particularly interesting or important life, or about a particularly interesting concept, it needs to be interesting to me.
sentences.zh: 无论它是关于某段历史的趣闻，还是关于某个有着特别有趣或重要人生经历的人，亦或是某个特别有趣的概念，它都必须能吸引我。

sentences.en: Secondly, it shouldn’t be about current affairs or a topic that will become irrelevant in weeks or months to come.
sentences.zh: 第二，它不应该是时事，也不应该是几周或几个月后就会过时的话题。

sentences.en: My hope is that anyone can go through our library of episodes and choose one that we might have made several years ago, but it will be just as relevant today as it was when it was made.
sentences.zh: 我希望任何人翻看我们的节目库，选择一期几年前制作的节目，它在今天依然和制作时一样有意义。

sentences.en: So something like King Henry VIII or Cleopatra - realistically, that isn’t going to change much, so it makes for a good candidate.
sentences.zh: 所以像亨利八世或克利奥帕特拉这样的话题——现实地说，这些内容不会有太大变化，所以是很好的选题。

sentences.en: And thirdly, it shouldn’t be about a highly controversial or divisive topic.
sentences.zh: 第三，它不应该是极具争议或容易引发分歧的话题。

sentences.en: I try to be as apolitical as possible in this show, within reason, and there are some topics that I know with complete certainty would end up flooding my inbox with angry messages on both sides of the argument.
sentences.zh: 我在节目中尽量保持政治中立，在合理范围内，我知道有些话题肯定会导致我的收件箱塞满来自辩论双方的愤怒信息。

sentences.en: I’m sure you can imagine what might fit into that category.
sentences.zh: 我相信你能想象出哪些话题属于这一类。

sentences.en: There are a few other things I take into consideration too, like whether a story can be properly told in an audio-only format.
sentences.zh: 我还会考虑其他一些因素，比如一个故事是否适合仅通过音频形式来讲述。

sentences.en: Some, like if you are talking about works of art or geographical borders, just don’t work quite so well without images, so I’ll also take that into consideration, and that’s the reason there aren’t many episodes about art.
sentences.zh: 有些话题，比如艺术品或地理边界，如果没有图像就没那么好理解，所以我也会考虑到这一点，这也是为什么关于艺术的节目不多的原因。

sentences.en: We also now make one three-part mini-series every month.
sentences.zh: 我们现在每个月还会制作一个由三部分组成的迷你系列。

sentences.en: Sometimes these will be about three different subjects that are all on a similar theme, but sometimes there will be a story that I just don’t think can be properly told in a single 20-minute episode, like the one on the Cambridge Five spy ring.
sentences.zh: 有时这些系列是关于同一主题下的三个不同话题，但有时是因为我觉得某个故事无法在 20 分钟内讲完，比如关于“剑桥五人组”间谍网的那期。

sentences.en: This started as a standalone, single episode, but I ended up splitting it into three different episodes, a three-part mini-series.
sentences.zh: 这最初是作为单集节目开始的，但最后我把它拆成了三集，做成了一个迷你系列。

sentences.en: So, once a topic is chosen, what next? Well, I’ll usually try to get as much of an understanding of the story or the topic as possible before writing anything down.
sentences.zh: 那么，选好主题后，下一步是什么？通常，在动笔写任何东西之前，我会尽量深入了解这个故事或主题。

sentences.en: This might start with something as basic as skimming over a Wikipedia entry to try to get an overview of the topic, before going into more detail about particular events or parts of the story, reading opinion pieces, downloading datasets and trying to make sense of them, reading books on the topic, it can be anything that helps me understand the topic better.
sentences.zh: 这可能从最基础的浏览维基百科词条开始，以获取主题概览，然后深入研究特定事件或故事片段，阅读评论文章，下载并分析数据集，阅读相关书籍，只要能帮我更好地理解主题，什么都可以。

sentences.en: Sometimes I start from a position of relative knowledge, if I’m writing about something I already know about.
sentences.zh: 有时如果我写的是已经了解的内容，起点就会高一些。

sentences.en: I started this show while living in Malta.
sentences.zh: 我是在住在马耳他期间开始做这个节目的。

sentences.en: I lived there for seven years and made several episodes about things related to Malta, so I was able to write most of those without too much prior research.
sentences.zh: 我在那里住了七年，制作了几期与马耳他有关的节目，所以大部分内容我不需要做太多前期研究就能写出来。

sentences.en: And I’ll often make episodes about people or historical events I’m already reading about, so I’ll be reading a book for fun, taking notes, and then when it comes to writing the episode of English Learning for Curious Minds, I just refer back to my notes, and the process is a whole lot simpler.
sentences.zh: 我还经常根据我正在阅读的人物或历史事件制作节目，比如我为了消遣读一本书，记下笔记，然后当要写 English Learning for Curious Minds 的脚本时，我只需参考笔记，过程就简单多了。

sentences.en: Once I feel relatively comfortable with my own knowledge of the subject, I’ll make a rough plan and start writing.
sentences.zh: 一旦我觉得对主题有了足够的了解，我就会制定一个粗略的计划并开始写作。

sentences.en: A rough plan for me is a very simple collection of five or so bullet points, with general ideas of how I want the episode to develop.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，粗略计划就是五条左右简单的要点，列出我希望节目如何展开的大致思路。

sentences.en: Sometimes it’s easy, like if it’s about the story of someone’s life, which typically follows a chronological order, but sometimes it’s harder, and it takes a bit more time and thought to get it right.
sentences.zh: 有时这很容易，比如讲某个人的生平，通常遵循时间顺序；但有时会比较难，需要更多的时间和思考才能理顺。

sentences.en: Then, I start writing. When I first started, I would write out general bullet points rather than the entire script, but when it came to recording, I found this meant I spent more time pausing and repeating certain parts in a different way, so now I write out the entire script, and I simply read it out loud.
sentences.zh: 然后，我开始写作。刚开始时，我只写大致的要点而不是完整的脚本，但在录音时，我发现这会导致我花更多时间停顿，或者用不同的方式重复某些部分，所以现在我会写出完整的脚本，然后直接朗读出来。

sentences.en: But I write as I speak, or at least I try to, so my hope is for an episode to sound more like a conversation, more like natural speech, than a formal written article read aloud.
sentences.zh: 但我我是按说话的方式来写的，或者至少我努力这样做，所以我希望节目听起来更像是在交谈，更像自然的表达，而不是在朗读一篇正式的文章。

sentences.en: As you can probably tell, I use a range of different vocabulary and expressions.
sentences.zh: 你可能已经察觉到了，我使用了一系列不同的词汇和表达方式。

sentences.en: There is no particular grand science to this, but I try to use language that someone at a B1 level could understand at a bit of a stretch, language that someone at a C1 level could understand almost entirely, but that anyone at B1 to C1 level will learn from.
sentences.zh: 这并没有什么高深的科学道理，但我尽量使用 B1 水平的人稍微努力就能听懂、C1 水平的人几乎能完全听懂，且 B1 到 C1 水平的人都能从中学习的语言。

sentences.en: This means not artificially dumbing down my language or using simple terms, but I might say something twice in two different ways — first naturally, and then in another, simpler way that will help you understand if you didn’t the first time.
sentences.zh: 这意味着我不会刻意降低语言难度或使用简单的词汇，但我可能会用两种不同的方式把一件事说两遍——先用自然的表达，然后再用另一种更简单的方式，如果你第一次没听懂，这能帮你理解。

sentences.en: I speak more clearly than I would if I were speaking to a native speaker, and of course, I make sure that all of the more complicated words and phrases are clearly defined in our transcripts and study packs.
sentences.zh: 我说话比对母语人士说话时更清晰，当然，我会确保所有较难的单词和短语在我们的文本和学习包中都有清晰的定义。

sentences.en: There are around 100 of these advanced words and phrases per episode, so that’s more than 50,000 different definitions created, and when you remove the duplicates, the ones that have appeared twice or more, there’s something like 20,000 B2 and above words that you’d learn if you listened to every episode.
sentences.zh: 每期节目大约有 100 个这类高级词汇和短语，所以我们已经创建了超过 50,000 条定义，如果去掉重复出现的词，如果你听完每一期节目，大约能学到 20,000 个 B2 及以上水平的单词。

sentences.en: Now, in terms of length, I aim to make each episode around 20 minutes long, with some coming in slightly under that and others a little over, which means the script should be between 2,500 and 3,000 words long.
sentences.zh: 在时长方面，我的目标是每期节目 20 分钟左右，有的稍短，有的稍长，这意味着脚本长度在 2,500 到 3,000 个单词之间。

sentences.en: I try to write the script in one go, and this writing process typically takes anywhere from two to five hours.
sentences.zh: 我尽量一气呵成地写完脚本，这个写作过程通常需要两到五个小时。

sentences.en: It’s rarely less than two, sometimes it can be much more than 5, but it tends to fall into that two-to-five-hour bracket.
sentences.zh: 很少低于两小时，有时会远超五小时，但通常都在两到五小时这个范围内。

sentences.en: Now, you might think this is quick, or you might think it’s a long time, but all I’ll say is that it used to take me a lot longer.
sentences.zh: 你可能觉得这很快，也可能觉得这很慢，但我只能说，以前花的时间要长得多。

sentences.en: After doing it 565 times and writing well over a million words, I've had quite a lot of practice, so it would be strange if I hadn’t got quicker.
sentences.zh: 在做了 565 次、写了超过一百万字之后，我已经有了大量的练习，如果还没变快那才奇怪呢。

sentences.en: And this brings me on to another important point.
sentences.zh: 这就引出了另一个重点。

sentences.en: At various points over the years, I have tried a bunch of things to speed up the process.
sentences.zh: 这些年来，我在不同阶段尝试过很多方法来加快进度。

sentences.en: I've experimented with hiring external scriptwriters to write episodes of English Learning for Curious Minds.
sentences.zh: 我曾尝试雇佣外部编剧来为 English Learning for Curious Minds 撰写脚本。

sentences.en: I posted a job for this once and got more than 500 applicants, and I trialled 30 different ones.
sentences.zh: 我曾为此发布过招聘信息，收到了 500 多份申请，并对其中的 30 人进行了测试。

sentences.en: Unfortunately–or perhaps fortunately–I never managed to find someone who was able to write to a level of quality that I was happy with, and that I felt was true to my voice and style, the voice and style of this podcast.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是——或者也可能是幸运的是——我从未找到能达到让我满意的质量水平，并且符合我的语气和风格，也就是本播客语气和风格的人。

sentences.en: In every case, when I would review the script that they had written, I found myself making so many edits and changes to their drafts, and starting to record an episode and realising that something they had written didn’t sound like me, that I realised it would have been quicker for me to just write everything from scratch.
sentences.zh: 每次我审阅他们写的脚本时，我发现自己要对草稿进行大量的修改，而且在开始录音时，我意识到他们写的东西听起来不像我，于是我意识到，还不如我自己从头开始写来得快。

sentences.en: So that is now what I do: no external scriptwriters, everything on this show is written by me, Alastair.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是我现在的做法：没有外部编剧，节目里的一切都是由我 Alastair 亲自撰写的。

sentences.en: I do, however, have another scriptwriting colleague, in the form of various AI models I use to help me at different points in the planning and writing process.
sentences.zh: 不过，我确实有另一位“编剧同事”，那就是我在策划和写作过程中不同阶段使用的各种 AI 模型。

sentences.en: Specifically, I primarily use ChatGPT, Claude and Grok, but I’ll sometimes use other tools as well for a second or third opinion on something.
sentences.zh: 具体来说，我主要使用 ChatGPT、Claude 和 Grok，但有时也会使用其他工具来获取第二或第三种意见。

sentences.en: During the planning stage, I will often tell ChatGPT what my proposed outline is, and ask it to point out areas I hadn’t thought about.
sentences.zh: 在策划阶段，我经常会告诉 ChatGPT 我的初步大纲，并让它指出我没想到的地方。

sentences.en: If I get writer’s block, and I’m just not sure where to go next in a script, I might paste in what I’ve written thus far and ask it to give me three different routes to take it next.
sentences.zh: 如果我遇到了写作瓶颈，不确定脚本接下来该怎么写，我可能会把已经写好的内容贴进去，让它给我提供三种不同的后续思路。

sentences.en: I don’t always use what the AI suggests, and if I do use them, I often find myself having to rewrite much of what ChatGPT provided, but they can be useful for giving me a fresh idea and helping me get back on track.
sentences.zh: 我并不总是采用 AI 的建议，即使采用了，我也经常发现必须重写 ChatGPT 提供的大部分内容，但它们在提供新鲜创意和帮我重回正轨方面非常有用。

sentences.en: I have, by the way, tested multiple times trying to get ChatGPT to actually write episodes in my voice.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一下，我多次尝试让 ChatGPT 真正用我的语气来写节目。

sentences.en: It does a better job than most of the human scriptwriters I've previously worked with, but it still sounds far too artificial, too unlike me, so I use it more as a sounding board, an editor and a review tool rather than a tool to write episode scripts.
sentences.zh: 它比我以前合作过的大多数人类编剧做得都要好，但听起来还是太假了，太不像我了，所以我更多地把它当作交流想法的对象、编辑和审阅工具，而不是直接写脚本的工具。

sentences.en: Now, when I've finished the draft of an episode, I’ll typically wait at least 24 hours, preferably more like two or three days, and then I’ll return to the script.
sentences.zh: 当我完成一期节目的草稿后，我通常会等待至少 24 小时，最好是两三天，然后再回过头来看脚本。

sentences.en: I’ll review it myself, spend a couple more hours making changes, and I’ll also paste the entire thing into two or three different AI tools and ask them to do everything from fact-checking to grammar checking, and to give me feedback on the narrative arc, things that I’ve missed, and so on.
sentences.zh: 我会自己审阅，再花几个小时进行修改，我还会把整个内容粘贴到两三个不同的 AI 工具中，让它们进行从事实核查到语法检查的所有工作，并对叙事结构、我遗漏的内容等提供反馈。

sentences.en: I don’t always act on the feedback, but it certainly is useful to have it there as a second or even third opinion, albeit a non-human one.
sentences.zh: 我并不总是根据反馈采取行动，但有这些非人类的第二甚至第三意见在，确实很有帮助。

sentences.en: And then, once I am happy with it, I’ll press record.
sentences.zh: 然后，一旦我满意了，我就会按下录音键。

sentences.en: I almost always find something I’m unhappy with during the recording process, so I have to stop the recording and rewrite that bit of the script before re-recording it, but once that is done, my work with the script is over, and it’s passed to our audio editor before being passed to our in-house teacher who creates all the in-line vocabulary definitions, and the accompanying study pack.
sentences.zh: 在录音过程中，我几乎总能发现不满意的地方，所以我不得不停止录音，重写那部分脚本，然后再重新录制。一旦录完，我的脚本工作就结束了，它会被交给我们的音频编辑，然后交给我们的内部教师，由他创建所有的文中词汇定义和配套的学习包。

sentences.en: And…that, I guess, is it. It isn’t a huge secret or special sauce, but rather the product of doing something more than 500 times.
sentences.zh: 差不多……就是这样。这并没有什么惊天大秘密或独门秘籍，而只是把一件事做了 500 多次的结果。

sentences.en: Still, there are many times when I listen to something again and think “eugh, I should have said that in a different way, or it would have been interesting to have talked about x instead of y”.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，很多时候我回听时还是会想：“哎呀，我本该用另一种方式表达的，或者如果聊 X 而不是 Y 会更有趣”。

sentences.en: I try not to listen to the episodes again, because I know that if I did this, I’d be constantly worrying about going back to change certain things, and that would mean that there wasn’t any time for making new ones.
sentences.zh: 我尽量不再回听节目，因为我知道如果我这么做了，我会一直纠结于回去修改某些地方，那我就没时间制作新节目了。

sentences.en: And I also now don’t really look too much at how many people listened to certain episodes, especially not on YouTube.
sentences.zh: 我现在也不太关注特定节目的收听人数，尤其是在 YouTube 上。

sentences.en: As you probably know, the algorithms on tools like YouTube and Spotify tend to gravitate towards clickbaity and extreme titles and subjects, so that’s why you see people making episodes about things like “10 English Words You Have To Know Today!” or “This Is Why You Can’t Speak English”.
sentences.zh: 你们可能知道， YouTube 和 Spotify 等平台的算法往往倾向于标题党和极端的主题，所以你会看到有人制作诸如“你今天必须知道的 10 个英语单词！”或“这就是你不会说英语的原因”之类的节目。

sentences.en: I know that I don’t want to make episodes about those sorts of things, and if I did, it would attract the wrong types of people to the show.
sentences.zh: 我知道我不想做那样的节目，如果我做了，会给节目吸引来错误的受众。

sentences.en: What’s more, I often receive emails from people telling me how much they enjoyed episodes that didn’t do nearly as well in terms of downloads, so I now pay very little attention to the download numbers.
sentences.zh: 此外，我经常收到听众的来信，告诉我他们有多喜欢某些下载量并不理想的节目，所以我现在很少关注下载数据。

sentences.en: What I do pay attention to, however, is what you, the wonderful listeners of this show and members of Leonardo English, tell me.
sentences.zh: 然而，我关注的是你们，也就是本节目的优秀听众和 Leonardo English 的会员们告诉我的反馈。

sentences.en: So let me finish this slightly meta episode by sharing some interesting facts from this big survey that hundreds of you were so kind to fill out at the end of July.
sentences.zh: 那么，在结束这期有点“元”的节目之前，我来分享一下 7 月底数百位热心听众填写的这份大型调查中的一些有趣事实。

sentences.en: So, the most popular countries in terms of listeners are Spain, China, Brazil, Italy and Germany.
sentences.zh: 听众人数最多的国家分别是西班牙、中国、巴西、意大利和德国。

sentences.en: Most listeners are over the age of 35. 69% of you say you listen for pleasure, while 47% list work as a reason.
sentences.zh: 大多数听众年龄在 35 岁以上。69% 的人表示听节目是为了乐趣，而 47% 的人将工作列为原因之一。

sentences.en: 75% of you also read books in English, and 66% of you watch TV or films in English.
sentences.zh: 75% 的人还会阅读英文书籍，66% 的人会看英文电视或电影。

sentences.en: Only 12% of you go to an English-language school.
sentences.zh: 只有 12% 的人在英语语言学校学习。

sentences.en: 71% of you listen to other English podcasts–well done–and 65% of you say your biggest challenge is speaking fluently, no surprise there.
sentences.zh: 71% 的人会听其他英语播客——做得好——65% 的人表示最大的挑战是流利表达，这并不意外。

sentences.en: I asked for feedback on how we could improve the show.
sentences.zh: 我征求了关于如何改进节目的建议。

sentences.en: There were some wonderful suggestions, but quite a few examples of the wide variety of people who listen to this podcast, and how you can’t please everyone.
sentences.zh: 有一些很棒的建议，但也体现了听众群体的多样性，以及众口难调的道理。

sentences.en: A bunch of you said you wanted more episodes about British society and culture, and about the same number of you said you wanted fewer.
sentences.zh: 一部分人说希望有更多关于英国社会和文化的节目，而同样多的人说希望少一点。

sentences.en: Almost as many of you said you wanted shorter episodes as said you wanted longer episodes, and there were as many of you who requested more complicated vocabulary as those of you who said you found it too hard to understand.
sentences.zh: 希望节目短一点的人和希望长一点的人几乎一样多，要求增加词汇难度的人和觉得太难听不懂的人也一样多。

sentences.en: We will, most probably, introduce some shorter episodes, and there are lots of more specific pieces of feedback that I’ll definitely be incorporating into the show, but these are just a few examples of how you can’t please everyone, and sometimes how you have to just do what feels right…
sentences.zh: 我们极有可能推出一些较短的节目，还有很多具体的反馈我肯定会采纳到节目中，但这些例子说明了你无法取悦所有人，有时你只能做你觉得正确的事情……

sentences.en: And very interestingly, of those of you who are members, 70% said you use your membership either every day or several times a week, which just goes to show that it really is very useful to many of you.
sentences.zh: 非常有趣的是，在会员听众中，70% 的人表示他们每天或每周多次使用会员服务，这说明它对你们中的许多人确实非常有用。

sentences.en: So, there we go, a peek behind the curtain, a look inside how these episodes are made.
sentences.zh: 好了，以上就是对幕后制作过程的揭秘。

sentences.en: I get pretty regular emails from people saying that they are thinking of starting a similar type of podcast in Spanish or French or Italian, and asking me for “the secret sauce” of how to do it.
sentences.zh: 我经常收到人们的来信，说他们想创办类似的西班牙语、法语或意大利语播客，并向我讨教制作的“秘诀”。

sentences.en: As you can see, there really isn’t a secret, but it’s the product of doing something pretty much every day for five years.
sentences.zh: 如你所见，真的没有什么秘密，这只是五年来几乎每天坚持做这件事的结果。

sentences.en: If you are thinking of starting a podcast like this in your own language — whether it’s Spanish, French, Chinese, whatever — my biggest piece of advice is just to start.
sentences.zh: 如果你正考虑用自己的语言——无论是西班牙语、法语、中文还是其他语言——创办这样一个播客，我最大的建议就是：直接开始。

sentences.en: Don’t worry if the first episodes aren’t perfect.
sentences.zh: 不要担心前几期节目不完美。

sentences.en: As you now know, mine certainly weren’t.
sentences.zh: 如你所知，我的前几期肯定也不完美。

sentences.en: And as a final thought, thank you for listening, and an especially big thank you to those of you who are members or who have ever bought a course or one of our products.
sentences.zh: 最后，感谢大家的收听，特别要感谢那些会员朋友，以及购买过课程或我们产品的人。

sentences.en: This show literally wouldn’t be possible without you.
sentences.zh: 没有你们，这个节目根本不可能存在。

sentences.en: OK then, that’s it for this meta episode on how I make podcast episodes.
sentences.zh: 好了，这期关于我如何制作播客节目的“元”节目就到这里。

sentences.en: I hope it was an interesting one, that you learned something new, and don’t worry, regular service will resume from the next episode.
sentences.zh: 希望这期节目很有趣，让你学到了新东西。别担心，从下一期开始，节目将恢复正常。

sentences.en: You've been listening to English Learning for Curious Minds by Leonardo English.
sentences.zh: 你正在收听的是由 Leonardo English 制作的 English Learning for Curious Minds。

sentences.en: I'm Alastair Budge, you stay safe, and I'll catch you in the next episode.
sentences.zh: 我是 Alastair Budge，祝大家平安，我们下期节目再见。
